summary:
ASTRA TRACK is a web-based platform that uses NASA's Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) to help people explore asteroids passing near Earth. I developed an interactive dashboard that displays real asteroid data, including estimated size, distance from Earth, and relative velocity. Users can search for objects and explore the information through the website.

The project addresses the challenge by making NASA's asteroid data easier to access and understand. Instead of requiring users to work with raw astronomical data, ASTRA TRACK presents the information in a clear interface that anyone interested in space can explore.

I built ASTRA TRACK because I wanted to make learning about asteroids more accessible and help people understand the objects that pass through our part of the Solar System.
details:
About ASTRA TRACK

ASTRA TRACK is a website that allows users to explore Near-Earth Objects using real data from NASA. It connects to NASA's Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs) and retrieves information about asteroids approaching Earth. The website presents this information in a dashboard where users can view estimated asteroid diameters, distances from Earth, relative velocities, and close-approach dates. Users can also search through the available objects to find specific asteroids.

The main benefit of ASTRA TRACK is that it makes astronomical information easier to access without requiring users to understand raw NASA data or have a background in astronomy. I wanted to create something that could help people become more interested in asteroids and understand why monitoring objects near Earth is important.

I developed the project using JavaScript and React for the website, Vite for the development environment, and Tailwind CSS for styling. I also used Node.js to build the backend, which communicates with NASA's API and handles requests from the website. The project is hosted on Render and its code is stored on GitHub.

What makes ASTRA TRACK creative is its mission-control-inspired interface, which presents scientific information in a way that feels interactive rather than like reading a database. During development, I considered the accuracy of the information, how easy the website would be to use, and how to keep the project accessible without requiring users to pay for access.
